rows.note: Use 大件 as the all-purpose choice for an object that is simply large or bulky.

example.english: This sofa is really bulky; once we put it in the room, there was no space left.
example.traditional: 呢張梳化真係好大件，擺入間屋即刻冇晒位。
example.jyutping: ni1 zoeng1 so1 faa2 zan1 hai6 hou2 daai6 gin6 baai2 jap6 gaan1 uk1 zik1 hak1 mou5 saai3 wai6

rows.note: Choose 笨重 when the size or weight makes something difficult to carry, move, or handle.

example.english: This washing machine is bulky and extremely hard to carry up the stairs.
example.traditional: 呢部洗衣機又笨重，搬上樓梯辛苦到不得了。
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 sai2 ji1 gei1 jau6 ban6 zung6 bun1 soeng5 lau4 tai1 san1 fu2 dou3 bat1 dak1 liu5

rows.note: Use 大隻 for a person or animal that is big-built, muscular, or notably large-bodied rather than for an inanimate object.

example.english: Look how bulky that security guard is; standing at the door, he looks imposing.
example.traditional: 你睇嗰個保安員幾大隻，企喺門口好有氣勢。
example.jyutping: nei5 tai2 go2 go3 bou2 on1 jyun4 gei2 daai6 zek3 kei5 hai2 mun4 hau2 hou2 jau5 hei3 sai3
